title: The Man Who Stopped a Nuclear War (1983)

segments.vo: In nineteen eighty-three, one man stopped a nuclear war.
This really happened.
September twenty-sixth, nineteen eighty-three. Just after midnight, in a secret bunker near Moscow.
segments.cap: September 26, 1983. Just after midnight, in a secret bunker near Moscow.

segments.vo: The officer on duty was Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov, watching the Soviet early-warning satellites.
segments.cap: The officer on duty was Lt. Col. Stanislav Petrov, watching the Soviet early-warning satellites.

scenes.sub: AIRLINER SHOT DOWN BY THE USSR

segments.vo: Weeks earlier, the Soviets had shot down a Korean airliner, killing all two hundred sixty-nine people aboard.
segments.cap: Weeks earlier, the Soviets had shot down a Korean airliner, killing all 269 people aboard.

segments.vo: Then the alarms went off.
A satellite had spotted an American intercontinental missile, heading for the Soviet Union.
segments.cap: A satellite had spotted an American intercontinental missile, heading for the Soviet Union.

segments.vo: Then four more appeared. Five missiles, inbound.
The satellites said attack.
But ground radar showed nothing at all.
segments.cap: But ground radar showed nothing at all.

scenes.quote: I had a funny feeling in my gut.

segments.vo: Petrov later said he had a funny feeling in his gut.
segments.cap: Petrov later said he had a funny feeling in his gut.

scenes.sub: A REAL FIRST STRIKE WOULD BE MASSIVE

segments.vo: Why would America start a nuclear war with only five missiles?
segments.cap: Why would America start a nuclear war with only 5 missiles?

segments.vo: He decided it was a false alarm, and no counterattack was launched.
segments.cap: He decided it was a false alarm, and no counterattack was launched.

segments.vo: So what had the satellites really seen? That's the strangest part.
segments.cap: So what had the satellites really seen? That's the strangest part.

segments.vo: The missiles were never real.
It was sunlight, reflecting off high-altitude clouds.
segments.cap: It was sunlight, reflecting off high-altitude clouds.

segments.vo: And his reward for saving the world? Nothing.
segments.cap: And his reward for saving the world? Nothing.

segments.vo: It stayed secret until after the Soviet Union fell.
segments.cap: It stayed secret until after the Soviet Union fell.

segments.vo: When he died in twenty seventeen, the world didn't notice for months.
segments.cap: When he died in 2017, the world didn't notice for months.
